extracted.intended_audience: general readers and journalists interested in the Claas Relotius case and journalistic ethics
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article documenting the Claas Relotius fabrication scandal; useful as a case study of journalistic fraud, verification failures, institutional response, and consequences for reporting practice. Extracts implied standards for credible journalism and newsroom oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not invent facts, persons, or quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: "falsified his articles on a grand scale, inventing facts, persons and quotations in at least 14 of his stories"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabrication is described as inventing facts, people and quotes (examples: made-up details in the Fergus Falls story; fabricated interviews with the parents of Colin Kaepernick). Such acts constitute gross journalistic fraud and are grounds for dismissal and revocation of awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear attribution and transparent sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: The awarded story was praised as "a text 'of unprecedented lightness, density and relevance, which never leaves open the sources on which it is based'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should clearly indicate and leave open the sources on which it is based; transparency about sources is an evaluative standard cited by award juries and is contrasted with Relotius's later revelations of fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough fact‑checking and co‑author/supervisor verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine uncovered the fraud after a co-author ... became suspicious of the veracity of Relotius's contributions and gathered evidence against him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-authors, editors and supervisors must verify contributions and follow up on inconsistencies or suspicions. Independent verification of facts, interviews and source material is a key guard against fabrication (example: Juan Moreno's investigation that exposed the fraud).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt, transparent institutional response to allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Der Spiegel left his articles accessible at the time, with a notice referring to the magazine's ongoing investigation into the fraud; later published a final investigation report and filed a criminal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should investigate allegations openly, inform readers of ongoing inquiries (e.g., leaving content accessible with notices), publish findings of internal investigations, and take appropriate legal or disciplinary steps when misconduct is confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No misuse of donations or funds; fundraising transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: He was accused of embezzling donations intended for Syrian orphans he claimed to have met in Turkey ... the donations were paid into his personal bank account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists soliciting or handling donations must ensure transparent, proper handling of funds; accepting charitable donations into personal accounts or misrepresenting beneficiary relationships is unethical and may be criminal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional accountability and need for editorial reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Der Spiegel's final investigation report ... stressed an urgent need for internal reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fraud or systemic failures occur, newsrooms must review and reform editorial, fact‑checking and oversight processes to prevent recurrence, even if initial findings indicate no broader complicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulating public information sources (no sockpuppetry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempts to manipulate and whitewash the German-language Wikipedia article on Claas Relotius ... were carried out by several newly created sockpuppets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists or their associates must not manipulate public records, encyclopedias or other reference sources using fake accounts; maintaining the integrity of public information is part of professional conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and recognition depend on integrity and can be rescinded
rubrics_metrics.description: Relotius received several awards for his reporting ... In the wake of the scandal, Relotius returned four awards ... and CNN revoked his 2014 Journalist of the Year award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition for reporting is contingent on honesty; discovered misconduct can lead to awards being returned or revoked and reputational consequences for individuals and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate, non‑sensational portrayal of people and communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Residents of Fergus Falls ... suspected that Relotius' portrayal of their hometown was inaccurate. 'In 7,300 words he really only got our town's population and average annual temperature correct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should avoid sensationalized or invented depictions of communities and subjects; on‑the‑ground claims must be verifiable and reflect the reality of the people and places described.
